why: The county labels place Kent above New Castle and Sussex, all bunched at mid-height, but New Castle is the northernmost county in the table (and the 3,291 m bridge is labelled as a ramp rather than the Delaware River crossing).
The 3,291 m bridge is labelled 'Mispillion River, 1939', but in the table the 3,290.6 m bridges cross the Delaware River and were built in 1951 and 1968.
The arc colours do not match the ratings: there is no rating-4 arc from 1920 or rating-3 arc from 1942, and the red arcs begin only in the 1960s.
The left map does not follow the table's coordinates: bridges at New Castle latitudes are spread out to the far eastern edge, so the outline of Delaware is lost.
Checked the rating counts (5/36/335/374/114/7/3), the oldest bridge (1839, Brandywine Creek), the arc colours by year (rating 4 in 1920, rating 3 in 1942) and the map's shape against the coordinates.
The rated-poor dots are in the wrong places: for example, the right panel has a dot at about 1992 and 39.66N, where the table has no poor bridge.
The arch widths do not follow length: the rated-poor 2,570 m C&D Canal bridge (1969, 39.56N) is drawn as a tiny arch.

The 'where' map has the wrong longitudes: the southernmost poor bridge (Assawoman Bay, SR 54, the most easterly in the table) is drawn mid-panel instead of at the eastern edge, and the map does not trace Delaware's shape.
The 'Delaware River 3,291 m, 1951' leader points to a glyph in the southern half of the map, but that bridge is at 39.69N in New Castle (the county labels are also piled together at the top).

Checked the 5-year histogram heights and colours (all-blue 2018 stack of 31), the Delaware River 3,291 m label, the colour of the rating-4 2,570 m bridge and the map positions, which fit the coordinates to within about 1 px.
It says the oldest bridge (1839) crosses 'SR 1 Milford bypass', but the 1839 bridge in the table crosses Brandywine Creek.
The map's longitudes do not match the table: New Castle and Kent bridges are spread across the full width to the far east, where the coordinates put none.
The county labels are stacked as Sussex, New Castle, Kent near 39.6N, but Sussex is the southernmost county (the poor-bridge dots are also misplaced).
The 3,291 m, 1951 bridge is labelled 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem', but in the table it carries I 295 N & US 40 E over the Delaware River.

The map glyphs' line weights do not follow ADT: some low-traffic bridges, such as 2418A418 with ADT 44, are drawn as heavily as busy ones (glyph weight barely correlates with traffic, unlike the correct rendering).
The map positions do not match the coordinates: bridges fill the whole width at every latitude, and the southern red (3-4) glyph sits mid-panel instead of at the eastern edge (Assawoman Bay).
The colours are wrong: the 2018 stack (all rated 7-8 in the table) is drawn orange and tan, and the rating-5 Delaware River bridge is drawn blue.

Checked all 10 rated-poor dots in both panels against latitude and year, the county counts (528/192/154), the earliest arches (1839, 1846, 1850, 1885) and the large rating-4 arch for the 2,570 m 1969 bridge.
The left map does not follow the coordinates: bridges are spread across a near-rectangle (for example, at the far east at New Castle latitudes) instead of tracing Delaware.
Checked the rating counts (41/335/374/114/7/3), '1965-1969: 88', the 5-year stack heights, the Delaware River 3,291 m 1951 label, the county counts and the map's shape.
